% Pattern: declaration/macro. \let\@defthm\newtheorem gives the declaration
% command another name, and \defthm calls it with two of its three arguments.
% Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want thm-1 statement/theorem 1
% want cor-1 statement/corollary 1
% want defn-1 definition 1
\documentclass{article}
\makeatletter
\let\@defthm\newtheorem
\def\defthm#1#2#3{\@defthm{#1}{#2}}
\makeatother
\newtheorem{thm}{Theorem}
\defthm{cor}{Corollary}{Corollaries}
\defthm{defn}{Definition}{Definitions}
\begin{document}
\begin{thm} Every compact space is bounded. \end{thm}
\begin{cor} Every finite space is bounded. \end{cor}
\begin{defn} A space is fine when it is compact. \end{defn}
\end{document}
